name: GHRP-6

track.title: Lab & animal

what.text: GHRP-6 is a lab-made chain of six amino acids, His-D-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2. It was described in 1984 as a small peptide that acts on the pituitary to release growth hormone, without releasing other pituitary hormones in those tests.

It acts through the same pituitary receptor as other growth hormone-releasing peptides. In pigs it raised the stress hormones ACTH and cortisol as well as growth hormone. In men it raised ACTH and cortisol during the night.

src.label: Raun et al., Eur J Endocrinol, 1998

what.text: GHRP-6 is not an approved medicine anywhere we checked. Using it for sleep has been studied only in two small one-night studies in healthy men.

research.text: GHRP-6 has been studied in people as a one-dose growth hormone test, in two small sleep studies, and, combined with epidermal growth factor (EGF), in stroke trials. The sleep studies found more light sleep but no more deep sleep.
Each study is listed below as it was run.

research.title: Night-time injections in healthy men, 1995

facts.v: four injections of GHRP-6 by vein during the night, compared with placebo
healthy young men (the abstract does not give the number)
single nights
sleep recordings, growth hormone, ACTH, cortisol

research.found: Growth hormone, ACTH and cortisol rose. Stage 2 (light) sleep rose from 245 to 270 minutes. Deep (slow-wave) sleep and other sleep measures did not change.

research.title: By mouth, nose or under the tongue, 1999

facts.v: GHRP-6 by mouth, by nasal spray or under the tongue, each compared with placebo
healthy young men (the abstract does not give the number)
single nights
sleep recordings, growth hormone, ACTH, cortisol

research.found: By mouth, hormones did not change. By nasal spray, growth hormone rose and light sleep tended to increase. The authors said the effects depend on dose, timing and route.

research.title: GHRH plus GHRP-6 test, 2000

facts.v: one dose of GHRH plus GHRP-6 by vein; 27 controls and all patients also had an insulin tolerance test
125 adults with pituitary disease and 125 healthy people
2 hours of blood sampling
peak growth hormone

research.found: The combined test separated people with growth hormone deficiency from healthy people, and the authors reported no side effects.

research.title: EGF plus GHRP-6 in acute stroke

facts.v: randomized, open-label, controlled; two dose groups vs standard care. Registered in the Cuban registry (RPCEC00000214).
36 adults with ischemic stroke, treated within 12 hours
twice daily for 7 days, followed for 6 months
safety; disability and function scores

research.found: Serious adverse events occurred in 9 of 16 in the standard-care group and in 3 of 10 and 2 of 10 in the treated groups. Two events in one treated patient were attributed to the treatment. Because GHRP-6 was given with EGF, its own effect cannot be separated.

research.title: COURAGE-2 stroke trial, 2026

facts.v: multicenter, randomized, open-label Phase III; EGF plus GHRP-6 vs standard care
188 adults with acute ischemic stroke
twice daily for 7 days; followed 6 months
disability (modified Rankin scale), survival, function

research.found: The trial missed its main goal: no differences in disability, function or survival overall. A subgroup with severe stroke did better. Serious adverse events occurred in 30 of 95 treated patients and 18 of 93 controls; the authors judged none treatment-related.

research.text: In rats, monkeys, lambs and calves, GHRP-6 released growth hormone. Given under the skin to young rats for 9 to 25 days, it increased weight gain. These results are in animals only.

us.text: Not FDA approved for any use. FDA placed GHRP-6 in Category 2 for outsourcing facilities (503B) on September 29, 2023, because it may present significant safety risks. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: none. A search of Drugs@FDA found no product with GHRP-6 as an active ingredient.

items.text: GHRP-6 was added on September 29, 2023. FDA says compounded GHRP-6 may pose a risk of immune reactions, and that "the available data reveal safety concerns including potential effect on cortisol and increase in blood glucose due to decreases in insulin sensitivity."

after.text: GHRP-6 is prohibited at all times (in and out of competition) under WADA class S2.2.4, growth hormone releasing factors. The class names "GH-releasing peptides (GHRPs) [e.g. alexamorelin, examorelin (hexarelin), GHRP-1, GHRP-2 (pralmorelin), GHRP-3, GHRP-4, GHRP-5 and GHRP-6]." All substances in class S2 are non-Specified. It is still named in the same class on the 2027 list, which takes effect January 1, 2027.

side.text: Safety data come from one-night studies, one-dose tests and short stroke trials where it was given with EGF. FDA flags effects on cortisol and blood sugar.

unconfirmed: The number of men in the 1995 and 1999 sleep studies is not given in the abstracts.
GHRP-6's regulatory status in Cuba, where the 2017–2018 stroke trial was run, was not checked with CECMED.
Status in the UK was not checked against a regulator record.
surprises: In the two small sleep studies we found, GHRP-6 increased light sleep and stress hormones, not deep sleep.
The largest trials of GHRP-6 are stroke trials in which it was always given together with EGF; the Phase III trial missed its main goal.
FDA flags GHRP-6 for effects on cortisol and on blood sugar through lower insulin sensitivity.
